% Text-mode commands that LaTeX accepts in math and MathJax lacks, set as in
% the PDF. \enskip, a space of half an em: in a display, in inline math,
% between \left( and \right) with subscripts, in a footnote, and inside
% \text, where MathJax knows it. \textsubscript and \textsuperscript, each
% a braced group of upright text: after a plain base, after a subscripted
% or superscripted base, before a superscript, in a theorem, and in a
% heading. \setcounter, \addtocounter, \stepcounter, and \refstepcounter,
% which draw nothing: in equation, equation*, and align*, before a matrix,
% and inside a matrix. \emph, \textsc, and \textsl as text in their font:
% in a numbered equation with a \kern inside, in inline math, and inside
% \text, where MathJax knows them. \textup and \textnormal, which MathJax
% knows, stay as they are.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsmath,amsthm}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\begin{document}
\section{Waves of speed $W\textsubscript{S}$}
Display:
\[ f \enskip g \]
Inline, $a \enskip b$, and in a numbered equation:
\begin{equation}
\left( h_{lm} \enskip k_{lm} \right)
\end{equation}
In text, $\text{c\enskip d}$.\footnote{In a footnote, $p \enskip q$.}

Subscripts: $V\textsubscript{P}$, $U_{0}\textsubscript{Q}$, and
$T\textsubscript{R}^{2}$. Superscripts: $x\textsuperscript{th}$ and
$y^{2}\textsuperscript{nd}$.
\begin{theorem}
The speed $Z\textsubscript{B}$ is finite.
\end{theorem}

Counters:
\begin{equation*}
\setcounter{MaxMatrixCols}{20}
\begin{matrix} m_1 & m_2 \end{matrix}
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
\begin{pmatrix} n_1 \setcounter{MaxMatrixCols}{20} & n_2 \end{pmatrix}
\end{equation*}
\begin{align*}
\setcounter{MaxMatrixCols}{20} r &= s
\end{align*}
\begin{equation}
\addtocounter{equation}{4} t = u
\end{equation}
\begin{equation*}
\stepcounter{equation} v = w
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
\refstepcounter{equation} e = o
\end{equation*}

Fonts:
\begin{equation}
x.\emph{of\kern0pt f}\sin x
\end{equation}
Inline, $\emph{ab}$, $\text{see \emph{cd}}$, $\textsc{gh}$, $\textsl{ij}$,
$\text{\textsc{kl} and \textsl{mn}}$, $\textup{op}$, and $\textnormal{qr}$.
\end{document}
